seen_animation: a.png shows a front-on, low-angle figure built from thin black lines: two wide arcs for the arms and shoulders that run from the frame bottom up and inward to the top, a U-shaped chin and jaw in the centre, and a pair of binoculars drawn as two looped eyepiece circles with slanted barrel tops held at eye level. An open hand with spread fingers sits on each side of the binoculars. Two grey clouds sit in the upper corners. Across frames 1-16 the figure stays in place. The whole body drifts slightly down and to the left and back over the shot, and from about frame 8 to frame 12 the binoculars and hands tilt a little, with the right eyepiece lower, before settling again in frames 13-16. No large action happens; it is a held pose of someone looking through binoculars, with a small sway.
seen_film: d.png shows a low-angle shot of a man in a blue padded jacket and dark cap holding black binoculars to his eyes with both hands, elbows raised wide, against a grey sky. Frame 1 is a dissolve from a previous shot (water and a shoreline show through). From frame 2 to 16 he holds the pose and looks up through the binoculars; the only motion is a small sway of the head, binoculars and shoulders, a slight tilt around frames 7-8 and small left-right and up-down shifts of the body. There is no change of action.
named_subject: A person looking up through binoculars held to the eyes with both hands (the binoculars are the doodle from c.png; arms, hands and chin are added in the same thin-line style).
evidence: Film f.png frames 2-29 are a held binocular pose with small sway; animation e.png frames 1-29 hold the same pose at the same place in the frame (binoculars at upper centre, arms arcing out to both lower corners, chin below the binoculars). g.png shows the drawings stacked in a tight, evenly graded band with no gaps or reversals: the arm arcs and chin shift a few pixels per sampled frame, matching the film's sway. The binocular tilt in e.png frames 12-16 corresponds to the small head tilt the film shows in its middle frames. Size stays constant across all frames; no doubling or redraws are visible in e.png. The film's frame 1 dissolve has no counterpart in the animation, which is acceptable since it is a shot transition, not the subject's action.
primary_gap: The hands are drawn as open, spread-finger palms standing beside the binoculars rather than wrapped around the barrels, so in still frames the figure can read as waving next to the binoculars instead of gripping them as the man in the film does.
closes_when: In every frame the fingers curl over the tops and outer sides of the two barrels (as in film frames 2-29, where the hands cup the binoculars from the sides) instead of pointing straight up beside them.
protect: The binoculars drawn exactly in c.png's construction (double-looped eyepieces with an inner loop, slanted open barrel tops, short bridge line); the thin single-weight line style of the added body; the low-angle framing with arms arcing to the bottom corners; the constant scale; and the small, continuous sway with no jumps.
identity_gap: The binoculars match c.png closely; the added arms, hands and chin are in a compatible thin-line style, though the spread-finger hands are more detailed than anything in the doodle.
